subject: forestSpirit
pitch: A small forest spirit, part deer and part mossy stone. A body of grey river stone covered in soft green moss, slender wooden legs ending in little hooves, branching antlers sprouting tiny white flowers and leaves, a pale wooden mask-like face with two glowing green eyes, and a few fireflies circling its head.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module built with the SDK, making sure every name is properly defined or imported so it runs cleanly. I'm envisioning a forest spirit creature with a mossy stone body, slender wooden legs, flowering antlers, a glowing-eyed wooden mask face, and fireflies circling its head.

Now I'm working out the proportions and skeleton -- shoulder and head heights, a spine chain from hips to chest sculpted with a faceted stone sweep painted in a grey-moss mottle, and leg joints positioned with hip/foot targets and limb lengths that reach the ground properly for the hooves.

I'm figuring out the leg joint structure: each leg is a two-bone chain with one bend direction, requiring three named points (hip, knee, tip) for a chain of two segments. I'm deciding to parent the hind legs to the hips joint and considering whether fore legs should parent to a chest joint instead.

For hooves, I'm placing a small cylinder at the foot position colored dark brown, attached to the tip joint of each leg chain. Then I move to the neck, building it as a curved chain from the chest up to a head joint, with tapering sweep radius and the same mossy stone color as the body, followed by planning a simple extruded face shape for the head.

Now I'm defining the head as a stone capsule with a pale wooden mask extruded from an outline shape on the front, specifying the outline's coordinate points to form a teardrop-like face, then adding mirrored glowing green eye spheres positioned using local head coordinates.

Now for antlers, I'm sprouting them from a surface point on the head using azimuth/elevation angles to find the base hit location, then building the branch as a curved catmull path from that base outward and upward to a tip.

For secondary tines branching off the main antler, I'm using sprout again but anchored to a frame along the antler's sweep path, with the tine's tip derived by offsetting that frame along a direction vector.

I'm picking a pale ivory-grey color for the antlers, then adding tiny white sphere "flowers" scattered along the antler path using stick, and planning to add leaf cards using small SVG textures at points along the antler frames, tinted green.

For the leaf shape I'm writing a simple SVG path for a rounded leaf filled with green. For the fireflies, I'm planning a ring of small glowing points circling the head, using part with a bright yellow-green color at each ring frame position.

Now I'm sketching the body structure: a hips root joint, a spine chain following a curved path with three named segments, and a swept body shape using a radius function to control width and height along the spine for a tapered, organic torso.

For surfacing, I'm blending stone and moss colors using mottling and countershading so the creature looks like weathered rock with patches of moss growth, defining hex colors for both.

I'm structuring the skeleton next: building a neck chain attached to the chest joint via a curved catmull path, then attaching a head joint at the neck's endpoint, defining positions and parent relationships for each joint.

For the head itself, I'm considering sweeping a short capsule-shaped path from the base to the top of the skull, with tapering radii and the head joint set as the bone reference, plus planning a mask piece on the front.

I'm also weighing whether to add a jaw joint for the mouth — the spec wants separate upper and lower jaws so it can open, but since this mask has no visible mouth, I'm leaning toward adding a simple jaw joint parented to the head with a small wooden chin piece, keeping the position and orientation lightweight rather than building a full articulated mouth.

Now I'm placing the mask itself, extruding it flush against the front of the head sphere at the right offset so its thickness centers properly on the drawn outline.

I'm recalculating the sphere geometry so the mask edges actually sit flush against the head's curved surface instead of floating in a gap — bumping head radius up and nudging the mask's center plane forward to close that offset.

Positioning the eyes using forward offset 0.18 from the head joint with small left/up adjustments relative to mask center. For antlers, I'm checking that surface attachment to the head joint works correctly, using the joint's position and an elevation angle to find a hit point on the skull surface, making sure the mask and eye geometry under the head bone don't interfere with that lookup.

I'm reordering the build so the surface query for antler attachment happens before the mask is added, avoiding interference. Then I'm sketching the antler path as a curved sweep from the hit point outward and upward with tapering radius, attaching tines via sprout with zero joint count but unique names to avoid conflicts.

Next I work out tine tip placement using offset vectors from points along the antler sweep, then plan small white sphere "flowers" stuck at those tips using along() to generate frames along the antler for placement, and sketch using similar frames for leaf cards.

Then I think about adding fireflies by generating a ring of frames around a central point for small particle effects.

Now I'm working through leg placement—figuring out hip socket positions for the hind and front legs relative to the body, and setting foot target coordinates so the legs land naturally beneath the body without splaying too wide.

With vertical reach roughly matching combined bone lengths, I'll use a small bend angle for each knee joint rather than a straight line, since real legs have a slight forward/backward bend. I'm using opposite bend directions for front versus hind legs to mimic how a deer's knees point forward while hocks point backward, then connecting the leg chains to their respective parent joints—hind legs off the hip root, front legs off the chest segment of the spine.

For the hooves, I'm placing a small cylinder at each foot joint's tip position, sized to taper slightly and sit near floor level. The legs themselves get swept geometry that tapers from a thicker top to a narrower ankle, giving a stick-like wood appearance, possibly using a faceted hexagonal cross-section for a more stylized look.

For coloring, I'm layering mottled stone and moss textures and using countershading to blend them across the body, neck, and head, with the head leaning more toward the stone tone. I'm also considering whether an unused import might trigger a lint error under strict TypeScript settings.

Settling on importing only what I actually use—frame, offset, catmull, mottle, countershade, and related utilities from the builder package, following the template's established import pattern. For the eyes, I'm placing them using the same local-offset object pattern shown in the documentation example.

Now I'm checking the geometry carefully: the eye spheres sit slightly forward of the mask's cutout plane, which looks like protruding glowing eyes rather than a clipping error. I'm tracing the head joint's position and orientation, confirming that using named directional words for placement keeps things consistent regardless of the joint's own rotation. Then I work out the head sweep's path and radius so the front of the head lines up closely with the mask, nudging the mask's forward offset slightly to get a cleaner flush fit with the eye spheres.

For the neck, I'm building a catmull-rom path through three points with two named joint spans, figuring out which joint in the resulting chain the head should parent to -- since the chain's joints are absolute positions, I just grab the last joint in the array to be safe rather than relying on indexing by name. Then I sweep the neck with a two-radius profile for consistent thickness, considering whether to pass a constant radius function instead of a fixed pair.

Now I'm thinking through the spine sweep profile, deciding against a tail for this creature, and sketching out moss tuft decoration -- scattering surface points on the body with a minimum distance and normal-based filter, then placing small leaf-blade SVG tufts at those points using the cards function, while noting I'll need an rng import for the scatter to be reproducible.

I'm also working out the antler sprout logic: getting a hit point on the head's surface using azimuth and elevation angles, checking for a null result before building the antler's catmull-rom path from that point upward and outward, and reasoning through what the hit's approximate coordinates should be given the chosen angles.

Then I'm planning the decorations along the antler — placing small flower spheres and leaf cards along its length using the along/stick/cards helpers, sizing the leaves appropriately. I'm also sketching out firefly rings around the scene with a warm yellow glow color, and considering adding subtle face details like cheek stripes or a small nose shape to round out the mask.

For the mask itself, I'm extruding a typed outline into a flat bone-anchored shape with bevel and smoothing, making sure to properly type the outline points. For the legs, I'm resolving how to reference the hoof joint at the tip of each leg chain, opting to index into the joints array directly rather than deal with nullable tip types, and now I'm ready to start writing the actual code.

Setting up imports and color palette...

Now I'm defining the hip joint and spine chain using a catmull spline, then sweeping the body mesh along it with a tapered radius function and octagonal cross-section. Moving on to defining the leg attachment points for each limb...

Writing leg helper function...

Setting hind and front leg bend directions and hip joint position, then moving to building the neck and head chain with Catmull-Rom spline points, sweeping tapered radii for the neck, and placing the head joint parented to the last neck segment with its own sweep using the coat material.

Now I'm adding a jaw joint under the head for subtle facial detail, then looping through both sides to grow antlers from surface-queried points on the skull, sweeping tapered antler geometry with hit points and spline curves. I'm sprouting small tines off each antler at specific points along their length with offset directions, adding flower buds and leaf cards scattered along the antlers, placing moss tufts across the body surface via scattered hits, positioning the eyes symmetrically on the head, extruding a mask shape over the face, and adding firefly particles in orbiting rings around the head—checking that all the coordinate math keeps everything proportioned on a roughly 2-meter deer-spirit frame. I'm also defining the leaf and moss tuft textures as small inline SVGs with simple colored shapes and strokes, then doing final sanity checks on sweep sections, paint colors, and point-type conversions before writing out the finished code.
